# opencode-trip-meter [![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/opencode-trip-meter)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/opencode-trip-meter) A trip meter for your OpenCode sessions: how fast the model is going and what the trip has cost so far. An [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) v2 plugin that adds two sections to the session sidebar: - **Speed**: output tokens per second for the last step, trailing time windows (5m and 1h by default), and the whole session. - **Price**: the selected model's price per million tokens for input, cached input, cache writes (when billed), and output, next to what the session has spent in each category. The Speed and Price sections appear below OpenCode's built-in Context section: ## Install opencode plugin add opencode-trip-meter Or add the package to `plugins` in `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`: ```json { "plugins": ["opencode-trip-meter"] } ``` ## Options Use the object form to change the trailing windows, in minutes: ```json { "plugins": [{ "package": "opencode-trip-meter", "options": { "windows": [1, 15, 60] } }] } ``` | Option | Default | Description | | --------- | --------- | ----------------------------------------------- | | `windows` | `[5, 60]` | Trailing windows for averaged speed, in minutes | ## How It Works Speed counts output and reasoning tokens per assistant step, timed from the first streamed part to the end of the model stream, so tool execution and time to first token are excluded. Prices come from the model catalog for the model selected in the prompt, using the base tier (context-size tiers are ignored). Models with no pricing, such as local ones, show the session's token counts per category instead, marked `no pricing`. Spend prices each message's tokens at the base tier of the model that produced it, so switching models mid-session stays accurate. Reasoning tokens bill as output. The total is checked against the costs OpenCode recorded for those messages; if they differ by more than 2% (tiered pricing, or a model missing from the catalog), a warning shows the billed amount and marks the breakdown as approximate. Spend covers this session's assistant messages only, not sub-agent sessions, so it can read slightly below the built-in Context total. ## Development Requires [Bun](https://bun.sh). bun install bun test bun run lint bun run build OpenCode loads plugin code from `node_modules` without the Solid JSX transform, so `bun run build` pre-transforms `src/` into `dist/` and keeps `solid-js` and `@opentui/solid` external so the plugin shares the host's runtime. `prepack` runs the build before `npm publish`. To try a local checkout, build it and symlink it into a project's plugin directory: bun run build mkdir -p /.opencode/plugins ln -s "$PWD" /.opencode/plugins/opencode-trip-meter ## Releasing Bump `version` in `package.json`, merge it, then publish a GitHub release tagged `v` (e.g. `v0.2.0`). The `publish` workflow checks the tag matches, runs lint and tests, and publishes to npm via trusted publishing, so no npm token is needed. ## Layout ```text src/index.ts no-op server part, so OpenCode loads the TUI part src/tui.tsx sidebar slot, history backfill, live first-token tracking src/stats.ts pure speed and pricing helpers tests/ bun tests for src/stats.ts scripts/ build script ```
